Draw one simple diagram: a straight track with A at x = 0, B at x = 40 m, C at x = 10 m, the car going A to B then back to C.

lines: Choose A as the origin and the direction toward B as positive. Position and motion depend on the observer's frame of reference; different observers can assign different velocities to the same car. The car travels A to B, reverses, then stops at C. Distance adds both path lengths and never becomes negative. Displacement is final position minus initial position; the return leg is negative in this frame. For any positive total elapsed time delta t, average speed is 70 m divided by delta t, while average velocity is +10 m divided by delta t. No numerical rate is available without the time. Instantaneous velocity is the signed derivative d x by d t; instantaneous speed is its the magnitude of v. While moving on the return leg, the car's velocity is negative.
देखो x equals 0 m initial position और origin है, इसलिए x A equals zero meters.
अब x equals 40 m turnaround position है, इसलिए x B equals forty meters.
और x equals 10 m final position है, इसलिए x C equals ten meters.
diagram का 70 m पूरे travelled path की length दिखाता है: D equals magnitude of forty minus zero plus magnitude of ten minus forty.
diagram का +10 m net change दिखाता है: delta x equals ten minus zero equals plus ten meters, यानी positive direction में.

diagram का 70 m पूरे travelled path की length दिखाता है: D equals magnitude of forty minus zero plus magnitude of ten minus forty.
diagram का +10 m net change दिखाता है: delta x equals ten minus zero equals plus ten meters, यानी positive direction में.

Cover: x against t graph, tangent slope as velocity, shapes for rest, uniform velocity and uniform acceleration; v against t graph, slope as acceleration, area as displacement, area below the axis negative; distance as total area ignoring signs; a against t graph, area as change in velocity; impossible graphs. Draw one simple diagram: a v against t graph rising from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s then flat to 10 s, with labelled v and t axes and its corner points marked. Do not shade any region. Label only the given values (20 m/s, 4 s, 10 s); explain the 160 m area in words.
lessons.opening: ठीक है... ये lesson motion graphs for jee from the basics के बारे में है. इसे basics से build करते हैं.
lines: Time runs horizontally and velocity vertically. Velocity rises steadily from zero to the marked corner, then stays constant along the flat segment. The slope of a velocity–time graph is acceleration. On a position–time graph, tangent slope is instantaneous velocity: a horizontal line means rest, a straight line with nonzero slope means uniform velocity, and a parabola represents uniform acceleration. Signed area under a velocity–time graph is displacement; area below the time axis is negative. Total distance adds the magnitudes of the areas. Signed area under an acceleration–time graph gives the change in velocity. The rising phase contributes a triangular area and the constant-velocity phase contributes a rectangular area. Together they give 160 m of displacement. Velocity never goes below zero here, so the distance is also 160 m. A graph cannot give one object two positions or two velocities at the same instant. In ordinary continuous motion, a position jump would mean teleportation, while an instantaneous velocity jump would require unbounded acceleration.

lessons.opening: ठीक है... ये lesson motion graphs for jee from the basics के बारे में है. इसे basics से build करते हैं.

lessons.question: A particle moves along the x axis. Its velocity against time graph is made of straight pieces joining these corner points in order: (0 s, 0 m/s), (2 s, 10 m/s), (6 s, 10 m/s) and (10 s, −10 m/s). Find the acceleration during the last piece, the displacement of the particle in 10 s and the distance it travels in 10 s.
lessons.opening: तो... ये question solve करते हैं. देखो question हमें क्या देता है.
lines: Read the four stated corners in time order. The last piece has acceleration minus 5 meters per second squared, its change in velocity divided by its four-second duration. Signed area under the graph gives displacement delta x equals 50 m. Adding the absolute areas gives distance d equals 70 m; the last piece has equal positive and negative triangular areas.

lessons.question: Explain non uniform acceleration using calculus for JEE from the basics. Cover: v = dx/dt and a = dv/dt for a given x(t); a = v dv/dx when acceleration depends on position or velocity; integrating a(t) with initial conditions; separating variables for a(v) such as a = −kv; rest instants and splitting distance at turning points. Draw one simple diagram: an x against t graph of x = t² from 0 to 4 s, and the tangent drawn at t = 2 s. Say the slope (4 m/s) in words, not as a label.
lessons.opening: अच्छा... ये lesson non uniform acceleration using calculus for jee from the basics के बारे में है. इसे basics से build करते हैं.

lessons.question: The position of a particle moving along the x axis is x = 2t³ − 9t² + 12t + 5, with x in metres and t in seconds. Find its velocity and acceleration at t = 3 s, the instants when it is momentarily at rest, and the distance it travels from t = 0 to t = 3 s.
lessons.opening: तो... ये question asks for its velocity and acceleration at t equals 3 s, the instants. पहले देखते हैं क्या दिया है.

A motorboat moving in a straight line at 20 m/s on a still lake switches off its engine. After that, its acceleration is a = −kv, where v is its velocity and k = 0.5 s⁻¹. Find its speed after it has travelled 30 m from the point where the engine was switched off, and the maximum distance it can travel.

lines: Show the stated initial speed, drag law, and 30 m displacement.

lessons.question: A motorboat moving in a straight line at 20 m/s on a still lake switches off its engine. After that, its acceleration is a = −kv, where v is its velocity and k = 0.5 s⁻¹. Find its speed after it has travelled 30 m from the point where the engine was switched off, and the maximum distance it can travel. Draw the boat's straight path with the switch off point, the 30 m point and the 40 m limit marked.

lines: अब 30 m आगे की position है, और x switch off से वहाँ तक travelled distance है. इस point पर x equals thirty meters.
Check करो: thirty meters पर relation में five meters per second मिलता है, और forty meters पर zero. इसलिए 30 m point, x max से पहले है: five greater than zero, और thirty less than forty.
raw: अब 30 m आगे की position है, और x switch off से वहाँ तक travelled distance है. इस point पर x equals thirty meters.

lessons.question: Explain relative velocity in one dimension for JEE from the basics. Cover: the velocity of A relative to B, v_AB = v_A − v_B, with one positive direction; subtract speeds for the same direction and add them for opposite directions; v_BA = −v_AB; relative displacement and relative acceleration; solving a crossing or a chase in the frame of one body. Draw one simple diagram: a straight road with east as positive, car A moving east at 20 m/s and car B moving east at 15 m/s. Label only the given 20 m/s, 15 m/s and the east direction; say the relative velocity of 5 m/s in words, not as a label.
lessons.opening: अच्छा... ये lesson relative velocity in one dimension for jee from the basics के बारे में है. इसे basics से build करते हैं.

lessons.question: Explain relative velocity in one dimension for JEE using this example: on a straight road, car A moves east at 20 m/s and car B moves east at 15 m/s. What is the velocity of A relative to B, and of B relative to A?
lessons.opening: ठीक है... इसे शुरू से समझते हैं.
lines: यहाँ v A car A की velocity है और v B car B की velocity है, और हमें निकालनी है v_{A over B} और v_{B over A}.
अब values डालो, v_{A over B} equals twenty minus fifteen meters per second.
तो under that assumption v_{A over B} equals plus five meters per second, यानी A, B से five meters per second east में आगे बढ़ता है.
values डालो, v_{B over A} equals fifteen minus twenty meters per second.
तो under that assumption v_{B over A} equals minus five meters per second, यानी A के frame से B five meters per second west में पीछे जाता हुआ दिखता है.
check करो, relative velocities antisymmetric होती हैं, तो v_{A over B} equals minus v_{B over A}, और plus five equals minus of minus five.
raw: यहाँ v_A car A की velocity है और v_B car B की velocity है, और हमें निकालनी है v_{A/B} और v_{B/A}.
अब values डालो, v_{A/B} equals twenty minus fifteen meters per second.
तो under that assumption v_{A/B} equals plus five meters per second, यानी A, B से five meters per second east में आगे बढ़ता है.
values डालो, v_{B/A} equals fifteen minus twenty meters per second.
तो under that assumption v_{B/A} equals minus five meters per second, यानी A के frame से B five meters per second west में पीछे जाता हुआ दिखता है.
check करो, relative velocities antisymmetric होती हैं, तो v_{A/B} equals minus v_{B/A}, और plus five equals minus of minus five.

lessons.question: Take east as the positive x direction. Train A is 120 m long and runs east at a steady 20 m/s. Train B is 180 m long and runs on a parallel track at a steady 10 m/s. (a) If B runs west, how long do the two trains take to cross each other completely, from the moment their front ends meet until their rear ends separate? (b) If instead B runs east ahead of A, how long does A take to overtake B completely, from the moment A's front end reaches B's rear end until A's rear end passes B's front end, and how far does A travel over the ground during this overtaking?
lessons.opening: ठीक है... ये question asks, how far does a travel over the ground during this overtaking. पहले देखते हैं क्या दिया है.

lessons.question: Explain river and boat problems for JEE from the basics. Cover: the boat's ground velocity is its velocity relative to the water plus the river velocity; the crossing time depends only on the component across the river, t = d/(v cos θ); least time by heading straight across, with drift u t; reaching the point directly opposite by heading upstream at sin θ = u/v, possible only when v > u. Draw one simple diagram: a river 100 m wide flowing east at 3 m/s, and a boat starting on the south bank heading due north at 4 m/s relative to the water. Label only the given 100 m, 3 m/s and 4 m/s; say the resultant speed and the drift in words, not as labels.
lessons.opening: ठीक है... ये lesson river and boat problems for jee from the basics के बारे में है. इसे basics से build करते हैं.

lessons.question: A stone is thrown horizontally with a speed of 40 m/s from the top of a vertical tower 80 m high standing on level ground. Take g = 10 m/s². How far from the foot of the tower does the stone hit the ground, and with what speed and at what angle below the horizontal does it strike the ground?
lessons.opening: तो... ये question solve करते हैं. देखो question हमें क्या देता है.
lines: A stone leaves an 80 m tower horizontally at 40 meters per second; g equals 10 meters per second squared.

The fall takes 4 s. The stone lands 160 m from the foot; its downward velocity component is 40 meters per second, so its impact speed is approximately 56 point 5 7 meters per second at 45 degrees below horizontal.

lessons.question: A ball is thrown from the edge of the flat roof of a building 40 m high with a speed of 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal, directed away from the building. Take g = 10 m/s². lines: A ball leaves the 40 m roof at 20 meters per second, 30 degrees above the horizontal; gravity acts downward.
देखो, h equals 40 m roof से ground तक building की vertical height है. Roof की height h equals forty meters.

lessons.question: A football is kicked from level ground with a speed of 20 m/s and lands 38.4 m away on the same level. Take g = 10 m/s², sin 37° = 0.6 and cos 37° = 0.8. Two different angles of projection give this range. Find both angles, and find the ratio of the maximum height on the lower path to the maximum height on the higher path.
lessons.opening: ठीक है... ये question solve करते हैं. देखो question हमें क्या देता है.
lines: Check करो: higher angle के लिए sine two theta equals two times zero point eight times zero point six, फिर zero point nine six ही आता है. इसलिए दोनों angles same range देते हैं, और lower path की height smaller है: sine(106 degrees ) equals 0 point 9 6; 7.2 m less than 12.8 m.
raw: Check करो: higher angle के लिए sine two theta equals two times zero point eight times zero point six, फिर zero point nine six ही आता है. इसलिए दोनों angles same range देते हैं, और lower path की height smaller है: sin(106°)=0.96; 7.2 m < 12.8 m.
